_about: PostgreSQL server-hardening and access rules VecShield evaluates for pgvector stores. Each rule names the condition it fires on (threshold), the severity, and the documentation it rests on; the quote is copied verbatim from source_url. The conditions themselves are code: posture/pg_hardening.py (server_hardening) and access/grants.py (access_grants) and access/isolation.py (tenant_isolation). A rule whose inputs the auditing role may not read is reported not observable, never as passed or failed.

server_hardening.title: pg_hba.conf admits non-local clients without authentication (trust)
server_hardening.threshold: a host, hostssl, hostnossl or hostgssenc rule that is not loopback-only has auth_method trust
server_hardening.quote: trust authentication is only suitable for TCP/IP connections if you trust every user on every machine that is allowed to connect to the server by the pg_hba.conf lines that specify trust.
server_hardening.remediation: Change the METHOD of every non-local pg_hba.conf line from trust to scram-sha-256, then SELECT pg_reload_conf().

server_hardening.title: TLS is off while the server listens on non-loopback addresses
server_hardening.threshold: ssl = off and listen_addresses names anything other than localhost or loopback addresses
server_hardening.quote: Enables SSL connections. This parameter can only be set in the postgresql.conf file or on the server command line. The default is off.
server_hardening.remediation: Set ssl = on with a server certificate and key in postgresql.conf, and use hostssl lines in pg_hba.conf for every remote client.

server_hardening.title: New passwords are stored as MD5 hashes
server_hardening.quote: Support for MD5-encrypted passwords is deprecated and will be removed in a future release of PostgreSQL.
server_hardening.remediation: Set password_encryption = scram-sha-256, then reset each role's password so it is re-hashed (ALTER ROLE <role> PASSWORD ...).

server_hardening.title: pg_hba.conf authenticates non-local clients with md5
server_hardening.threshold: a non-loopback host rule has auth_method md5
server_hardening.quote: The method md5 uses a custom less secure challenge-response mechanism.
server_hardening.remediation: Re-hash passwords with password_encryption = scram-sha-256, then change those pg_hba.conf lines to scram-sha-256.

server_hardening.title: pg_hba.conf accepts clear-text passwords from non-local clients
server_hardening.threshold: a non-loopback host rule has auth_method password
server_hardening.quote: The method password sends the password in clear-text and is therefore vulnerable to password “sniffing” attacks.
server_hardening.remediation: Change those pg_hba.conf lines to scram-sha-256.

server_hardening.title: Statement logging writes chunk text and embeddings to the server log
server_hardening.quote: Logged statements might reveal sensitive data and even contain plaintext passwords.
server_hardening.remediation: Set log_statement = ddl (or none) and log_parameter_max_length = 0; record data access with pgaudit object logging, which can omit parameters, instead.

server_hardening.title: pgaudit writes statement parameters (chunk text, embeddings) to the audit log
server_hardening.threshold: pgaudit is loaded, pgaudit.log_parameter = on, and pgaudit.log records read, write or all
server_hardening.quote: Specifies that audit logging should include the parameters that were passed with the statement. When parameters are present they will be included in `CSV` format after the statement text.
server_hardening.remediation: Set pgaudit.log_parameter = off, or restrict the audit log's readers as you restrict the vector tables.

server_hardening.title: Non-superuser login roles can read every role's statement text
server_hardening.threshold: pg_stat_statements is installed and a login role that is not a superuser has the privileges of pg_read_all_stats (the auditing role itself is excluded)
server_hardening.quote: For security reasons, only superusers and roles with privileges of the pg_read_all_stats role are allowed to see the SQL text and queryid of queries executed by other users.
server_hardening.remediation: REVOKE pg_read_all_stats (and pg_monitor) from roles that do not monitor the server; pg_stat_statements normalises most constants, but the text still shows table and filter structure.

server_hardening.title: The server accepts TLS versions below 1.2
server_hardening.threshold: ssl = on and ssl_min_protocol_version is TLSv1 or TLSv1.1
server_hardening.quote: The default is TLSv1.2, which satisfies industry best practices as of this writing.
server_hardening.remediation: Set ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.2' (or TLSv1.3) in postgresql.conf and reload.

server_hardening.title: No audit logging extension records who read the vector tables
server_hardening.threshold: shared_preload_libraries is readable and does not load pgaudit
server_hardening.quote: The PostgreSQL Audit Extension (pgAudit) provides detailed session and/or object audit logging via the standard PostgreSQL logging facility.
server_hardening.remediation: Add pgaudit to shared_preload_libraries, restart, CREATE EXTENSION pgaudit, and enable object logging for the vector tables (pgaudit.role).

access_grants.title: The retrieval role is a superuser, or can become one
access_grants.threshold: the retrieval role has rolsuper, or is a member of a role that has it
access_grants.quote: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.
access_grants.remediation: Create a dedicated login role for retrieval with SELECT on the vector tables only, and connect the application as that role.

access_grants.title: The retrieval role bypasses row-level security on a vector table that relies on it
access_grants.threshold: a vector table has row security enabled and the retrieval role has rolbypassrls, or is a member of a role that has it
access_grants.quote: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.
access_grants.remediation: ALTER ROLE <retrieval role> NOBYPASSRLS, and revoke membership in any role that has BYPASSRLS.

access_grants.title: The retrieval role owns a vector table whose row security does not apply to its owner
access_grants.threshold: a vector table has row security enabled, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY off, and is owned by the retrieval role
access_grants.quote: Table owners normally bypass row security as well, though a table owner can choose to be subject to row security with ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
access_grants.remediation: ALTER TABLE <table> FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or better, retrieve as a role that does not own the table.

access_grants.title: The retrieval role can change the vector tables it reads
access_grants.threshold: the retrieval role holds INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on a vector table
access_grants.quote: Allows INSERT of a new row into a table, view, etc.
access_grants.remediation: REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON <table> FROM <retrieval role>; give ingestion its own role.

access_grants.title: The retrieval role can create and administer roles
access_grants.quote: A role with CREATEROLE privilege can alter and drop roles which have been granted to the CREATEROLE user with the ADMIN option.
access_grants.remediation: ALTER ROLE <retrieval role> NOCREATEROLE; administer roles from a separate account.

access_grants.title: Every role can read a vector table that has no row security
access_grants.threshold: PUBLIC holds SELECT on a vector table with row security disabled
access_grants.quote: The special “role” name PUBLIC can be used to grant a privilege to every role on the system.
access_grants.remediation: REVOKE SELECT ON <table> FROM PUBLIC, and GRANT SELECT to the roles that retrieve.

access_grants.title: Any role can create objects in a schema the vector extension or the search path uses
access_grants.threshold: PUBLIC holds CREATE on the vector extension's schema or a schema in the session's search_path
access_grants.quote: To implement this pattern, first ensure that no schemas have public CREATE privileges.
access_grants.remediation: REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA <schema> FROM PUBLIC (PostgreSQL 15 and later already do this for public in new databases).

access_grants.title: VecShield audited as a role that bypasses row security
access_grants.threshold: the connecting role has rolsuper or rolbypassrls
access_grants.quote: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.
access_grants.remediation: Audit as a least-privileged role (docs/pgvector.md); isolation results then show what an application role sees.

access_grants.title: Row security on an approximate index can make searches come back short
access_grants.threshold: a vector table has row security enabled, its vector column has an HNSW or IVFFlat index, and the effective <index>.iterative_scan for the retrieval role is off
access_grants.quote: With approximate indexes, queries with filtering can return less results since filtering is applied after the index is scanned.
access_grants.remediation: ALTER ROLE <retrieval role> SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order (IVFFlat: ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order); pgvector 0.8.0 or later. Never fix short results by retrieving as a role that bypasses row security.

tenant_isolation.title: Filtered searches on an approximate index can come back short
tenant_isolation.threshold: a collection shared by two or more tenants is searched through an HNSW or IVFFlat index whose effective <index>.iterative_scan is off
tenant_isolation.quote: With approximate indexes, queries with filtering can return less results since filtering is applied after the index is scanned.
tenant_isolation.remediation: ALTER ROLE <app role> SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order (IVFFlat: ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order); pgvector 0.8.0 or later.
